findings.description: The async `__ror__` flattens using `isinstance(other, retry_all)`, but it is defined on the async `retry_any`, so the check should be against `retry_any`. The base-class version in tenacity/retry.py correctly checks `retry_any`. Here `retry_all.retries` are merged into a `retry_any`.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `retry_all(a, b) | async_retry_any(c)`. The code runs `retry_any(a, b, c)`, so the AND-group is flattened into an OR. A retry that should fire only when both a and b hold now fires when a alone holds. This silently changes retry behavior. `retry_all` here is the async class (the name resolves at call time), and `retry_any` and `retry_all` are separate classes.
